attributes.residual: BASELINE CORRECTION AND THE LOAD-BEARING STRUCTURAL FINDING: the function's 433/433 'count-exact' status was a COINCIDENCE of cancelling per-block deltas, not alignment. Per-block accounting from the --ops insert/delete/replace list at baseline: mode-2 +2 (an extra address copy plus an extra 4882 rematerialisation), mode-5 -1, mode-1 -1, net 0. The work claim's dichotomy ('433 count-exact at real 504 = either massive renaming or displaced-slot content') was therefore false on both horns: there is no slot displacement at all, and roughly half the gap was ordinary source-reachable structure hiding under a cancelling count. FOUR NAMED RESIDUALS REMAIN, each reduced to a specific mechanism. (1) mode-2 @0x25c, the only surviving count-positive cluster: target emits 'add r18,r28,r21' straight into a callee-saved register for 'row = &tblB[i]'; ours emits 'add r3,...' into a volatile and then pays 'addi r22,r3,0' to preserve it across the two calls. Two probes (block-local vs function-scope pointer) produced byte-identical output, so declaration scope is not the lever; this is register-assignment choice at the def site. (2) mode-2 tail @0x368 and mode-4 tail @0x644, population 2, count-neutral: for 'for (k = 0, i = 0; ...)' the target emits two independent 'li rD,0' while ours emits one 'li' plus an 'addi rD,rS,0' copy (MWCC value-numbers the two zeros and coalesces). PROVEN NOT SOURCE-FORM-REACHABLE WITHOUT A PROBE: mode-3's tail loop uses the byte-identical source form 'for (k = 0, i = 0; k < 3; k++, i += 12)' and MATCHES, so the divergence is context/pressure dependent, not a property of the loop spelling - do not spend probes respelling these loops. (3) mode-5 @0x3cc/@0x3f0, count-neutral after the mode-1 work: the LICM hoist described under probed_form; the target's shape implies the original variable has a use the hoist cannot absorb, which no tried spelling reproduced. (4) mode-4 @0x608 divwu-vs-addi: the pre-existing scale-divisor cap from v2, re-screened and NOT re-probed. WHY THE FUNCTION STILL CANNOT FLIP: regnorm on the improved object reports 211 RENAMING rows with the callee-saved block r16-r25 mapping NON-BIJECTIVELY (every one of r16..r25 flagged INCONSISTENT, e.g. ours r20 -> target r17x12/r18x11/r16x7), so the whole-function recolor is not a renaming any WebFrank rule can discharge - verify_consistent_recolor would refuse, and the residual is not the pure-recolor subclass the audit scans. The renaming, not the four clusters, is now the dominant term in real.
